ownership_and_budget.list_metadata: The lazy PreparationQueues object holds the first participating Plan's exact metadata_owner and compilation_storage ref. Its SmallVector uses that exact plan.allocator. Entries are declared last, so their Queue objects and vector allocator storage are destroyed before the retained budget and metadata owner.
ownership_and_budget.allocation_lifetime: A budget allocator allocation retains StorageBudgetState itself, while the added explicit budget/metadata-owner references also protect the unallocated/empty-list and raw-allocator cases. No new queue/container allocation is performed for artifact hits or nonqueued factories.
ownership_and_budget.family_scope: The sole product by-value ConstantArtifactCache lives inside compile_family. Shared parent/child compilation receives the same family compilation_storage. The CompileEnvironment and prepared artifacts preserve the existing owner contracts around map destruction. The new list does not become Plan runtime state or a global Context pool.
ownership_and_budget.charges: Existing provider resident/transient declarations and reserve_private paths are unchanged. The new endpoint-list metadata goes through the original Plan allocator; backend Queue resources retain their original Context ownership. This review does not claim that native queue/event allocation has zero cost or that every backend-private byte is separately measured.

endpoint_identity_and_ABA.key: ContextRef::identity_key is the actual ContextState address, independently of provider/target slots or device IDs.
endpoint_identity_and_ABA.retention: A cached Queue owns a QueueState, whose constructor retains ContextState and whose destructor releases it only after backend Queue and QueueState storage destruction. A nonempty reusable slot therefore prevents its endpoint address from being recycled for a different Context.
endpoint_identity_and_ABA.empty_slots: Failure moves the Queue out and leaves an empty slot. Even if a later Context eventually obtains the same historical identity address, that slot contains no Queue and creates a new Queue from the current actual endpoint. Raw identity values are compared, never dereferenced.
endpoint_identity_and_ABA.closed_context: queued_preparation_supported checks the current Context is open. Queue::is_open additionally checks Queue and Context admission. A closed moved-out Queue is discarded before replacing it, and a Context closure during admission produces an error instead of cached reuse.

success_and_error_paths.success: The Queue is moved out of the vector before QueueSequence::begin. Only factory success, sequence finish, attached-retention wait success, owned nonempty payload validation, map insertion and remember returning kPrepared allow move-back. is_open is checked again before move-back.
success_and_error_paths.factory_error: A rejected status is recorded on the original sequence. Accepted work still completes through the original finish/Completion retention path. Even a known-retired failed episode is intentionally discarded; it cannot poison or replace a cached success for another endpoint.
success_and_error_paths.finish_or_observation_error: No return-to-cache branch is reached. The original local Queue destructor closes admission and releases its owner without introducing a drain. Existing Completion::settle hands unknown retirement and its attachment to backend destruction. ConstantPreparationState retains the original Plan, artifact and transient charge until the backend's real retirement callback releases them.
success_and_error_paths.partial_payload_or_remember_error: An unowned/empty payload, insertion failure or remember failure returns before move-back. A successfully prepared payload that was inserted before a remember error may remain in the existing artifact cache until normal prune/retry; the failed acquisition's Queue is still discarded.
success_and_error_paths.candidate_transition: begin_candidate and commit_plan retain original payload prune/accounting logic. They do not reset successful preparation queues. An empty failed slot creates a fresh Queue for that endpoint on a later miss while the other endpoint's successful Queue remains intact.
success_and_error_paths.completion_body: The finish/retention/wait body itself is unchanged in changes.diff. No delayed wait, merged sequence, new host drain or new retirement policy was introduced.

new_tests: QueuedPreparationReusesTwoInterleavedComputeEndpoints: two distinct real CPU Contexts and owned resources, A/B/A/B misses, exactly two retained QueueState identities, successful reuse across a candidate transition, original Queue admission closed by Cache destruction.

QueuedFailureDiscardsOnlyItsOriginalEndpointQueue: accepted synchronous CPU prefix followed by a factory tail error, payload destruction, only that endpoint Queue closed, next candidate creates its replacement while the other endpoint retains its original Queue.
test_review.identity_witness: QueueWitness uses the existing exported retain/release functions and retains actual QueueState objects; allocator address recycling cannot turn recreation into a false reuse assertion. It does not instantiate private QueueState::destroy across the Compute binary boundary.
test_review.existing_unknown_retirement: The existing GraphPacking.UnknownPreparationObservationRetainsOwnersUntilNativeRetirement source explicitly exercises one/two failed observations with asynchronous mock native retirement, drops caller owners and failed compile state, and checks allocator/resource/context/payload/transient-budget retention until the original native retirement callback. Source presence is not a claim that root has rerun it in this batch.
test_review.limits: The new CPU tests alone do not exercise real CUDA queue events, an asynchronous unknown-retirement failure, injected endpoint-list allocator failure, or a tracked metadata allocator lifetime for this new list. Those properties are source-reviewed above; actual regression/runtime observations must be reported separately without claiming new tests cover them.

review.maintainability: The addition is one private lazy endpoint-owner list in the existing cold ConstantArtifactCache. It reuses original Queue/QueueSequence/CompletionLifetime rather than adding a scheduler, public configuration, global pool, new executor or copied native algorithm.
review.build_refresh_review: constant_artifact.cc owns definitions; executable.cc is the sole product by-value/stack Cache owner; constant_artifact_cache_test.cc owns test by-value caches. Other declaration-only includers need no artificial rebuild solely for this private class-layout addition.
review.performance_claim: None. Actual event/queue counts and cold-prepare timing require root's separate real-consumer evidence.
